effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per field or layout rule of the Mantle Transaction Encoding specification, in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in logos-blockchain-core or logos-blockchain-binary-codec that fails on 0.3.0 for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Logos Blockchain is a Rust workspace (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.lock committed). Package names carry a `logos-blockchain-` prefix the directory names lack; the `name` field of each crate's Cargo.toml is authoritative. The audited ref is the release tag 0.3.0 (commit 1da2d9d69a80452cf6b5d0e68304762d510c8a6c); record the resolved commit in the report. The specification in the prompt is the LIP as published in the logos-lips repository at commit fddc2c1 (the 2026-10-08 Bedrock snapshot). The five RFC appendices that propose changes to this encoding are separate documents audited by their own briefs.

The document defines the byte layout of a Mantle transaction and of every operation and proof it carries: field order, widths, endianness, length prefixes, and what the transaction hash is computed over.

Where the encoding lives in the code:
- core/src/mantle/transactions/codec.rs (package `logos-blockchain-core`): the transaction encoder and decoder. src/mantle/ops/serde_.rs: per-operation encoding, including the opcode byte. src/mantle/ops/op.rs and ops/op_proof.rs: the operation and proof payload types whose fields are laid out. src/mantle/transactions/hash.rs: the bytes the hash covers.
- binary-codec/src and binary-codec/macros/src (packages `logos-blockchain-binary-codec`, `logos-blockchain-binary-codec-macros`): the generic wire codec (integer widths, endianness, length prefixes, collections) the Mantle codec is built on; the Network Wire Format LIP that defines it is audited by another brief, so cite a divergence in the generic codec as belonging there and trace here only what the Mantle layout requires of it.

Running tests: the gate runs the unit's packages with cargo-nextest, which is what CI uses (`.github/workflows/code-check.yml` runs the whole workspace that way; the whole workspace is too large for this container, so the gate is narrowed to the unit). `cargo nextest run --locked -p <package> --all-features` runs one package; `cargo test --locked -p <package> --all-features -- <filter>` works too. `.config/nextest.toml` marks a unit test slow after 30 s and kills it after 2 min. ZK proof dependencies come as prebuilt circuit crates (`lbc-*-sys` with the `prebuilt` feature) and the verifier links rapidsnark statically, so the first build compiles C++ and takes a while; nothing needs a running node, docker, or downloaded circuit files. New proof tests go in the owning crate's tests/ directory or as a `#[cfg(test)]` module file under src/ named by finding id; the core crate's existing codec tests and core/src/mantle/fixtures/ show how an encoded transaction is asserted byte for byte. Treat code comments that cite a spec paragraph as claims to check.
